sections.content: ARTICLE I - RECOGNITION

Pursuant to the Certification of Representative, issued by the National Labor Relations Board in New York University and United Staff Association of NYU, Local 3882, New York State United Teachers, AFT, AFL-CIO, Case No. 2-RC-18155, New York University recognizes the United Staff Association of NYU, Local 3882, New York State United Teachers, AFT, AFL-CIO, as the sole and exclusive bargaining agent for all full-time and regular part-time office clerical employees in Code 106, and all full-time and regular part-time laboratory/technical employees in Code 104, including those employees receiving tuition remission, and all "special" employees who have been employed for at least twelve (12) consecutive weeks and have worked an average of twenty hours or more per week. Excluded from the unit are all employees in Codes other than 104 and 106, Medical Center employees, full-time students, work-study students, students receiving financial aid through New York University, casual employees, confidential employees, professional employees, guards and supervisors as defined in the National Labor Relations Act.

sections.content: ARTICLE II - CHECKOFF

Upon receipt of an employee's written authorization, which shall not be irrevocable for more than one (1) year, or beyond the termination of this Agreement, whichever occurs sooner, the Employer shall deduct from such employee's salary in accordance with this Agreement, such employee's Association dues and remit same to the duly authorized representative of the Association each month, together with a list of the names of the employees from whose salary deductions were made. Such a written authorization may be revoked by the employee by written notice to the Employer and the Association during the ten-day period prior to the end of any such applicable yearly period or during the ten-day period prior to the termination date of any applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement, whichever occurs sooner. In the absence of such notice of revocation, the authorization shall be automatically renewed for an additional yearly period or until the end of the Collective Bargaining Agreement, whichever occurs sooner. The deduction shall be made in the first paycheck of the month. The Employer agrees to transmit the dues deducted to the Association by the tenth (10th) day of the following month. The Association shall have the exclusive right of dues checkoff for all employees covered by the recognition clause of this Agreement.

ARTICLE III - PROBATIONARY PERIOD

Each employee shall be on probationary status during the first three (3) months of employment, excluding time lost for sickness and other leaves of absence. During or at the end of the probationary period, the Employer may discharge any such employee and such discharge shall not be subject to the grievance and arbitration provisions of this Agreement. Extensions of the probationary period may be agreed upon by the Employer and the Association.

sections.content: ARTICLE IV - TEMPORARY EMPLOYEES

Employees hired to fill a specific job for less than three (3) months shall acquire no seniority and be deemed temporary employees.
If such employees are retained in the same position after three (3) continuous months, they shall be classified as permanent employees, and receive seniority credit and all other benefits as provided in this Agreement, as would an employee who had completed his/her probationary period. These three (3) months shall serve as said employee's probationary period.

category_summaries.summary: New York University recognizes the United Staff Association of NYU, Local 3882, NYSUT, AFT, AFL-CIO as the sole and exclusive bargaining agent for (i) all full-time and regular part-time office clerical employees in Code 106, (ii) all full-time and regular part-time laboratory/technical employees in Code 104, and (iii) “special” employees who have been employed for at least twelve (12) consecutive weeks and have worked an average of twenty (20) hours or more per week. The Employer will deduct Association dues from employees’ salaries pursuant to the Agreement and remit the deducted amounts to the Association each month by the tenth (10th) day of the following month; deductions require receipt of authorization cards by the Employer’s designated representative, are not retroactive, and employees may revoke written authorization by written notice to the Employer and the Association. The Association has the exclusive right of dues checkoff for covered employees. The University will provide the Association specified unit information, including names of newly hired members (home addresses, work locations, Social Security numbers, date of employment, codes, grades, and salaries), notices of certain personnel actions (dismissals, layoffs, resignations, deaths, promotions, demotions, transfers) including dates and—where applicable—home addresses, as well as complete and annual lists of bargaining unit members by name and by order of date of hire.

The duration of the agreement runs through October 31, 1982, and the agreement is intended to remain effective until either that date or, if earlier, the termination of the applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement, whichever occurs sooner. After the initial term, it renews for successive irrevocable one-year periods unless revoked in writing by the employee to the University’s Director of Personnel Services. The Association may act during the ten-day period prior to the end of the yearly period or prior to the expiration of the applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement. The parties also agree to commence negotiations for a successor contract upon request of either party on or after August 1, 1982, and the contract documents refer to a collective bargaining agreement covering clerical and laboratory technicians (American Federation of Teachers Local #3882), which was stated to have expired October 1981. Standard severability and legal-supremacy language provides that invalidity due to conflict with applicable federal, state, or local law does not affect the remaining provisions.

The agreement preserves management’s exclusive prerogatives, including the right to operate and manage the University and to supervise and direct employees. Management may select and hire employees, and may suspend, discipline, demote, discharge for cause, promote into supervisory or other positions, and assign, transfer, supervise, and direct the workforce. The University also retains the authority to maintain discipline and efficiency, determine facilities, methods, means, equipment, procedures, and personnel, promulgate rules and regulations, and exercise customary management functions. Temporary employees may be hired while a permanent employee is being sought. Employees must actually perform duties that are assigned at the Employer’s request, and any employee engaging in prohibited conduct is subject to disciplinary action (including discharge) at the Employer’s discretion.

Compensation provisions include overtime and work-hour payments: at the Employer’s discretion, hours above the base workweek but not exceeding 40 hours may be paid, and hours over 40 per week are paid at time-and-one-half. Employees on payroll on November 2, 1981 and covered by the Agreement receive a 10% increase in base rate, with no reduction in pay. Pay for changes in job grade or assignments is addressed: if a job grade is instituted outside the listed structure, the job rate is negotiated with the Association; employees temporarily assigned to a higher-rated bargaining unit job for 20 workdays or more are paid no less than the minimum rate for that job or an additional $5.00 per week (at least as specified); if employees bump more than one grade, they are paid at the rate of the employee bumped, or, at the Employer’s discretion, a rate not to exceed the maximum for the grade; for a vacant position, the rate is the position rate plus 10%, and the Employer may, at its discretion, pay a higher rate. Holiday pay requires time-and-one-half for all hours worked on specified holidays (including December 28, 1981 and December 30, 1981 during the 1981–82 academic year) in addition to straight-time pay, or alternatively allows the Employer to choose straight-time pay in addition to straight-time holiday pay, or an additional day of straight-time pay; permanent part-time employees receive straight-time for hours they would have been scheduled to work on University holidays. For layoffs, severance is provided: upon severance due to layoff, all permanent full-time and part-time employees receive a severance allowance equal to one-half, paid on a separate check.

Scheduling provisions address how employees’ hours and work assignments are determined and communicated. Employees hired after the specified date will have their hours fixed at the time of hire, and nothing in the agreement guarantees work or the number of hours in the workweek. The parties also provide for overtime/premium pay limits, stating that under no circumstances may overtime or any premium pay be calculated at a rate greater than time and one-half the regular rate. The agreement applies prior to the applicable September 1 or within thirty (30) days of the effective date, whichever occurs later. Schedules may vary by area based on operational needs, but the total number of paid holidays remains the same; permission for scheduling-related needs will not be withheld unreasonably. Employees must be given a minimum of five (5) days’ notice if they are required to work on a holiday, and holiday work will be assigned by requesting volunteers from among fully qualified employees. Employees are expected to report for work if they can return in time to perform at least three (3) hours within their normal schedule, and employees are guaranteed their normal length lunch period.

The agreement provides paid holiday benefits for all permanent full-time employees, including paid holidays scheduled on regular workdays and eight (8) additional paid holidays per academic year (September 1–August 31). Eligible employees must be regularly scheduled to work the holiday and generally must work both the regularly scheduled workday immediately preceding and following the holiday to receive holiday pay, with limited exceptions for absence due to illness/injury with sick-leave pay (and physician certification may be required) or where the employee is on previously scheduled vacation/personal holiday/other holiday, jury duty, or is entitled to bereavement pay for the relevant days. Employees are paid for the holiday (not charged to vacation) and, with the supervisor’s prior approval, additional vacation days may be scheduled/added. Holiday pay is denied if the holiday falls during a leave of absence, after the employee’s last day worked, or on the first working day after the scheduled expiration of the employee’s leave; employees on disability or workers’ compensation benefits are also not eligible for holiday pay. Separately, personal holidays are discretionary with the Employer and require advance mutual/supervisor approval, may be refused during peak periods and are limited to not more than one per six-month portion of the academic year, are subject to probation requirements for new hires, and are not available to terminating employees or payable in lieu.

For the duration of the agreement, healthcare coverage is provided without cost to employees for applicable premium sharing, with the University continuing its contributions (including reducing employee/family contributions effective deductions after December 1, 1981 from $7.00/month to $5.00/month, while the University continues $16.60/month). Blue Cross family coverage extends to unmarried full-time students’ ages 19 to 23, and the same extension applies to sponsored children. Part-time permanent employees may enroll in Blue Cross and the Equitable Basic Physician plan, and may enroll in University-participating HMO plans at their own expense. The University contributes the same dollar amount toward the cost of selected coverage; any difference between the University contribution and the selected coverage cost is paid by the employee. Equitable Major Medical applies with a $100 per-person deductible per calendar year (maximum three per family), a $250,000 lifetime maximum payment per person, and Equitable Basic Physician providing 100% reimbursement up to “Reasonable and Customary” charges for surgical services. Annual medical examinations are available upon request to full-time permanent employees for a $25 fee. The University also continues health (and life) insurance contributions during periods of leave, while the employee must continue paying their share of premiums if applicable.

The Employer will maintain the New York University Staff Pension Plan for eligible bargaining unit employees for the term of the Agreement. Eligibility requires reaching age 25, completing 12 months of University employment, and working 1,000 hours in a consecutive 12‑month period; employees hired on or after age 60 are not eligible. The pension benefit is calculated as (average monthly salary over the last five years prior to the termination date) × 0.008 × credited years of service (capped at 35 years), and service credit accrued after an employee’s 65th birthday is not counted. Normal retirement occurs on the first day of the month following the month of the 65th birthday (or on the birthday itself if it falls on the first of the month). Effective November 1, 1981, credited years of service include service prior to the month the employee attained age 22.

Security-related employment protections provide for an initial three (3) month probationary period for new employees, during which the Employer may discharge employees without the grievance/arbitration rights under the Agreement; the probation period may be extended by agreement of the Employer and the Association. Temporary coverage is limited: employees hired for less than three (3) months receive no seniority and are temporary, but if retained after three (3) continuous months they become permanent and receive seniority and other Agreement benefits. Permanent vacancies cannot be filled through a series of temporary employees. Seniority governs layoffs and recalls: laid-off employees may transfer and, if displaced, may exercise University-wide seniority by “bumping” a less senior employee in a lower rated title, with only one bump allowed and the most junior employee in the target title being bumped (bumped employees cannot bump others). For Code 104 employees, bumping into a lower-paid title requires filling vacancies or bumping the most junior employee in that title, and salary reductions are capped to the extent the current salary exceeds the bumped employee’s rate plus 10%. Employees displaced into the same grade/job title may be assigned at their former rate and retain applicable pay increases occurring within six (6) months of layoff; recalled employees return at former rate plus any across-the-board increases for up to six (6) months after layoff. Seniority rights cease upon voluntary resignation, failure to return from leave, failure to accept recall within eight (8) working days after notice sent (by certified mail) to the employee and Association, or layoff exceeding six (6) consecutive months; for layoffs over six months, the vacancy/job is filled by the most senior applicant who responds within eight (8) working days of notice. The Association must be notified one week prior to permanent layoff, and permanent bargaining unit job vacancies are posted for five (5) working days before being filled, with applicants considered during that window. Additional job security provisions include: periodic written job descriptions and their review/issuance, an assignment/transfer process for volunteer-based work using greatest/least seniority depending on volunteer sufficiency, retirement at the first day of the calendar month on/after the 70th birthday, and severance protections stating that a recalled employee treated as new has future severance based only on service accrued after recall, with severance of one-half (1/2) week’s pay per full year up to thirteen (13) weeks and termination grounds for failure to return at the end of approved leave.

Disputes must be resolved solely under the Agreement’s grievance and arbitration procedures (Article XXVI), and if the parties do not agree, the matter is handled under that Article. Grievances may be filed by the aggrieved employee or the Association within fifteen (15) days of the grievance’s occurrence (otherwise deemed waived). Employees must first discuss the grievance with the immediate supervisor (who may involve Personnel Services); a Shop Steward may be present. The supervisor responds within ten (10) days, and if denied, the Association may appeal to Step 2 within ten (10) days of the Step 1 denial, submitting a written grievance with reasonable particularity to the designated administrative official (with a copy to Personnel Services). If not adjusted, the Association may appeal to Step 3, with Employer/Association meetings occurring within five (5) days and the Employer issuing a written decision within ten (10) days of the Step 3 meeting (or the Employer may initially present at Step 3). A discharge or suspension contest requires written notice to the Employer within eight (8) working days; if no complaint is filed within that time, the action becomes final. Disputes not involving the interpretation, application, or claimed violation of a specific Agreement term are not grievable. Time limits exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays; failure to answer at any step does not constitute acquiescence, and the Association may proceed to the next step. Grievances reaching arbitration may be taken within fifteen (15) days of the Step 3 response; the parties request arbitration, and the arbitrator’s jurisdiction is limited to grievances, with no authority to alter the Agreement’s terms. Arbitration fees/expenses are shared equally. Certain matters are excluded: neither the Association nor employees may grieve job content/description; employees disciplined under this Article have no recourse to the grievance/arbitration procedures; discharges or suspensions not timely contested are final; and the arbitrator cannot rule on subjects reserved for negotiation, and must not rely on provisions for unrelated arbitration purposes.

Safety-related provisions require that neither the Employer nor the Association discriminates against any present or future employee in violation of applicable Federal, New York State, and New York City laws, including on grounds such as race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental disability, or membership/non-membership in the Association. Additionally, if an employee is absent for more than five (5) consecutive work days, the employee must undergo a medical re-evaluation, and the Employer may require the employee to take a medical examination.

Miscellany provisions include: employment-related reporting—monthly submission of information reports, stating unchanged employment status when applicable, and timely sharing with the Association of University-wide rule, regulation, and Personnel Manual changes affecting terms and conditions (sent at the same time as distribution); identification and notices—communication of Social Security No. and provision of six (6) bulletin boards (24" x 36") in reasonably accessible locations for Association notices regarding meetings, dues, entertainment, and general union activities; employment documentation—job descriptions must include the title(s) of the employee’s immediate supervisor(s); examinations—an examination fee of $30; labor relations—no lockout by the Employer; no call/authorization of members for prohibited activity by the Association, with immediate efforts to stop any unauthorized work stoppage or violation (including notice distribution to employees and the Employer within twelve (12) hours), confirmed by an Association officer’s signed statement to terminate immediately; bargaining—each party agrees it is not obligated to bargain collectively; and authorization—one report is authorized by law under 29 U.S.C. 2.
